title: Satin density 0.1 lines/mm on a 40 x 6 mm column: crossings on every line once two lines would span more than the sawtooth period limit
description: A 40 x 6 mm rectangle sewn as satin across the 6 mm (Direction 90 degrees), under sewing off, density 0.1 (PE-DESIGN's minimum): the lines lie 10 mm apart; PE-DESIGN's sawtooth, whose diagonals normally span two lines, puts a crossing on every line here, so each half is a vertical crossing, an 11.7 mm diagonal to the next line, a vertical crossing, the walk along the far edge to the start point's line and the crossing down to the start point (36 stitches in all, the longest 11.66 mm; a two-line diagonal would be 20.9 mm).

featureMatrix.feature: Satin: a zigzag across the column

evidence.note: PE-DESIGN 11.50 reference compat/reference/stitches/sweep-satin-density-min.pes (2026-10-27): status bar 39 stitches, 36 as the harness counts them; crossings at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 mm from the page's left edge (x = 100..500 in 0.1 mm), every diagonal 11.66 mm. The rule is a spacing, not a stitch length: region-travel-u-satin keeps 30 mm diagonals over two lines at 4.5 lines/mm. Two lines are skipped at 3 lines/mm (0.67 mm) and not at 0.1 (20 mm); OpenStitch stops skipping above a 10 mm period. To pin the limit: the same column at density 0.15, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5 (two lines span 13.3, 10, 6.7 and 4 mm).

references.make: On a 100 × 100 mm Design Page (grid 1 mm, Snap to Grid) draw a 40 × 6 mm rectangle with the Rectangle tool from (10, 10) to (50, 16) mm. Line Not Sewn; colour 800 RED; region sew type Satin Stitch, Direction Manual straight line 90°, Under sewing unticked, Density 0.1, Pull compensation 0.0 mm, Half Stitch at its default, every other attribute at PE-DESIGN's default. Save with Save As as PES (PE-DESIGN 11's default PES version) under the file name given, and record the PE-DESIGN version, the date, the operating system and every setting you changed in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json (see docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md).
